question.text: Assume Saraswati Growth Fund (Cat II trust) incurred a BUSINESS LOSS of INR 10 crore in FY 2024-25 (pre-FA 2025 period, on a stream characterised as business income). Under Section 115UB, how is this loss treated?

answer.text: Passed through to LPs pro rata, to be set off against their own business income.
Passed through to LPs but only if they have held units for 36 months.
NOT passed through to LPs; carried forward at the FUND level to be set off against business income of subsequent years, subject to the general 8-year carry-forward rule for business losses.
Forfeited — business losses of an AIF cannot be carried forward at all.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 115UB specifically provides that BUSINESS LOSSES of an Investment Fund are NOT passed through to unitholders. Such losses are retained at the fund level and carried forward for set-off against future business income of the fund, subject to the general carry-forward rules (Section 72 — up to 8 assessment years immediately succeeding the year of loss). Only NON-business losses are passed through (and only to LPs holding units ≥12 months). **The Trap:** Option A wrongly passes business loss through. Option B invents a 36-month holding requirement — the 12-month rule applies only to non-business losses. Option D forfeits the loss entirely, which is incorrect. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same split: business loss stays at fund; non-business loss passes through. XIX-A uses it in LP-advisory talking points. XXI-B does not apply — no trust, no pass-through gymnastics. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a fund historically prone to business-income characterisation (e.g., high-churn Cat II debt strategies pre-FA 2025), track the business-loss carry-forward file separately at fund level — it's a real asset on future tax returns, and an acquirer of GP stake may factor it into their valuation.
